cards.explanation: The answer is a tomb for himself. God asks Shebna who authorized him “…to carve out a tomb for yourself here…” (Isaiah 22:16). He's up on the height with a chisel, picking out his own resting place in the rock. That's a lot of rock for one man to plan around, friends.

The answer is a wide land. God says He'll sling Shebna into it, and then adds, “There you will die…” (Isaiah 22:18). Notice the tomb Shebna was carving on the height isn't mentioned as the place. The text just says a wide land, and I'm not going to guess past that.

The answer is True. God says Shebna will die in a wide land, and “…there your glorious chariots will remain—a disgrace to the house of your master.” (Isaiah 22:18). Glorious chariots, and they end up a disgrace. That's quite a drop, friends.

The answer is that he'll be removed from office. God says, “I will remove you from office, and you will be ousted from your position.” (Isaiah 22:19). He says it twice, in two different ways, so there's no mistaking it. Shebna's time as steward is done.

The answer is Shebna's robe and sash. God says, “I will clothe him with your robe and tie your sash around him.” (Isaiah 22:21). He also puts Shebna's authority in Eliakim's hand. It's a hand-me-down, friends, but a pretty important one.

The answer is Judah. God says Eliakim “…will be a father to the dwellers of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah.” (Isaiah 22:21). Father to the dwellers of Jerusalem and the house of Judah? Sounds like a job with no days off.

The answer is False. God says, “What he opens no one can shut, and what he shuts no one can open.” (Isaiah 22:22). It works both ways, and nobody can undo what Eliakim does with that key. The key goes on his shoulder, friends, and I can't even keep track of my spatula.

The answer is firm. God says, “I will drive him like a peg into a firm place…” (Isaiah 22:23). A peg only works if it goes into something solid. Then the verse adds another picture: “…he will be a throne of glory for the house of his father.”

The answer is his family's descendants and offshoots. The text says they'll hang on him “…all the glory of his father’s house: the descendants and the offshoots…” (Isaiah 22:24). It also lists the lesser vessels, from bowls to every kind of jar. That's a whole household hanging from one peg, friends.

The answer is that it will give way and fall, and it's a surprise after all that firm talk. The LORD of Hosts declares, “…the peg driven into a firm place will give way; it will be sheared off and fall…” (Isaiah 22:25). The text doesn't say more about why, so I'll leave it right there, friends. And it ends with “Indeed, the LORD has spoken.”
